name: EXPRAG / Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience (incl. EXPRAG-LoRA)
venue: ICLR 2026 Workshop on Memory for LLM-Based Agentic Systems (MemAgents), OpenReview id=HXTOSwUwF6, published 03 Mar 2026 (CC BY 4.0). A preprint exists at arXiv:2603.18272 (2026-03, NAVER LABS Europe). The PDF header reads 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026', but the OpenReview venue listing is the ICLR 2026 MemAgents workshop. The term 'EXPRAG' itself was coined by contemporaneous work Wei et al. 2025 (Evo-Memory, arXiv:2511.20857) and adopted by this paper.
authors_affiliation: Thomas Palmeira Ferraz, Romain Deffayet, Vassilina Nikoulina, Hervé Déjean, Stéphane Clinchant. All authors at NAVER LABS Europe, Meylan, France. Correspondence: thomas.palmeira@naverlabs.com, stephane.clinchant@naverlabs.com.
code_url: N/A (no official code repository found for this paper; the only public 'EXPRAG' implementation is in the separate Wei et al. Evo-Memory benchmark repo github.com/zhaosnw/evo_mem, which is a different work that coined the term) [uncertain]
task_domain: LLM-agent sequential decision-making in text-based interactive environments (embodied/decision-making). Evaluated on embodied household manipulation (ALFWorld) and science-experiment tasks (ScienceWorld). Not QA/tool-use; the work explicitly distinguishes itself from Agentic RAG (knowledge-intensive QA) and positions itself as retrieval-augmented AGENTS retrieving experience to improve decisions.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, multi-turn decision making in fixed text-based environments where dynamics are fixed but required action sequences differ across tasks. The central goal is robust generalization to UNSEEN tasks within the same environment, including action types not observed during training (e.g., trained to clean an object but tested on heating one). Supervision is available as scripted expert trajectories from the environment-provided policy (these include failures/suboptimal segments). The agent is a moderately-sized open LLM adapted with supervised LoRA fine-tuning. The work systematically studies three settings: (1) training-free experience retrieval at inference (EXPRAG), (2) supervised LoRA fine-tuning (LoRA baseline), and (3) retrieval-augmented fine-tuning (EXPRAG-LoRA) that injects the retrieved memory block into each training context. The memory is intentionally a FIXED, read-only bank of full trajectories (no online write/update/reflection). For out-of-distribution (hard) tasks, a small set of in-domain reference trajectories (expert demos or strong-model rollouts) is assumed collectable for the index.
what_is_retrieved: Past full interaction TRAJECTORIES (experiences). Each retrieved item is a complete agent trajectory tau = (T, o1, a1, ..., o_{T-1}, a_{T-1}, o_T) serialized as a multi-turn chat. Stored as raw chat-formatted data (including successful and unsuccessful episodes), and retrieved as in-context exemplars. No documents, skills, guidelines, or reflective summaries are retrieved.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory in spirit, but operationally a FIXED read-only episodic experience bank built offline. Retrieval targets prior interaction trajectories (episodic memory) rather than a static semantic corpus of documents/KB/APIs. The paper explicitly contrasts classic RAG (external semantic memory = corpus) with its episodic-memory view (retrieve prior trajectories to guide action selection). The bank is built offline from expert trajectories of the relevant task split and NOT updated online during deployment.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-K nearest-neighbor ranking objective. The agent retrieves the top-K most relevant trajectories by dot-product similarity (K in {1,2,4}; K=2 chosen as default efficiency-effectiveness tradeoff). No completeness/minimal-set objective and no variable-size precision-driven recommendation; selection is fixed-K and the study analyzes how K affects performance ('more experiences vs. context rot').
retrieval_unit: full trajectory: a complete agent rollout (task description + observation/action turns) stored as raw chat-formatted data. Trajectories are stored without filtering or aggregation; the retrieval and injection unit is the whole trajectory (one trajectory per retrieved item, K of them assembled into a memory block).
index_source: Growing-in-spirit but FIXED episodic memory, offline-induced: the retrieval index is built from scripted expert trajectories generated by the environment-provided policy on the training split (including failures unless stated otherwise). For fine-tuning, only successful trajectories from the training split are used as supervision; the index includes both successful and unsuccessful episodes. Index is split-specific (easy/hard/all) and not grown online at test time. For OOD tasks, a small in-domain reference set (expert demos or strong-model rollouts) is assumed collectable.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index: a Sentence-Transformers embedding store of trajectory key embeddings e_i = phi(tau_i), queried by nearest-neighbor (dot-product) search. No graph, hierarchical, or cluster organization. The index can be composed by task-type partition (easy/hard/all) but within a partition it is a flat embedding index. Trajectories stored as raw chat-formatted (OpenAI message) data.
retriever_type: Dense (embedding-based) nearest-neighbor retriever using the Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B model (Zhang et al. 2025c) via the Sentence-Transformers library; top-K retrieved by dot-product similarity in embedding space. Off-the-shelf, frozen embedder (no other embedding model was tried). Not BM25/learned/generative/LLM-as-retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf): the trajectory encoder phi is a fixed pretrained Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B model and is kept frozen throughout the paper; the authors found retrieved trajectories satisfactory given the simplicity of the retrieval task. There is no contrastive fine-tuning, LM-feedback, RL, preference, or downstream-task-effectiveness training of the retriever. (The POLICY is trained via LoRA, and EXPRAG-LoRA trains the policy to better USE retrieved context, but the retriever itself is never trained.)
query_construction: Two regimes. Static: the query q_t is built from the current task description (raw task text) once at episode start. Dynamic: the query is rebuilt at every step from the current agent context = task description + partial interaction history h_t, requiring re-encoding the prompt with updated retrieved examples. No query decomposition, intent extraction, or synthetic expansion; the query is the formatted text of the (task / task+history).
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/state-level depending on mode. Static retrieval = task-level (one-shot at t=0 using the task description). Dynamic retrieval = step/state-level (re-query at every decision step using the growing interaction history). The fine-tuning experiments adopt static (task-level) retrieval as the default.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot (static, default) OR iterative/per-step (dynamic). Static retrieves once at episode start and keeps the memory block fixed for the whole episode; dynamic re-retrieves on a fixed schedule at every step. Both are FIXED-schedule, not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router.
retrieval_trigger_signal: fixed schedule: retrieval fires unconditionally either once at t=0 (static) or at every decision step (dynamic). There is no token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned-complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated trigger; the WHEN is a hard-coded static-vs-dynamic schedule chosen as an experimental variable.
reranking: None. After dense top-K nearest-neighbor (dot-product) retrieval, the K trajectories are assembled directly into the memory block; no cross-encoder, RRF, hierarchy-aware, or instruction-tuned reranking stage is applied.
retrieved_context_refinement: Light formatting only, no semantic refinement. Retrieved trajectories are inserted verbatim into a memory block (prepended to the system prompt) that separates successful from unsuccessful demonstrations; within it they are serialized in 'chat JSON' format by default (ablated against agentic JSON, compact JSON, and textual). No compression, decomposition-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, or distractor filtering is performed; the model itself must learn to identify which retrieved actions are relevant (failures are deliberately kept in the index).
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation (in-context) plus, in EXPRAG-LoRA, a training signal. At inference, the top-K trajectories are formatted into a memory block m_t = system(tau^1,...,tau^K) prepended to the policy prompt, and the LLM policy pi_theta samples the next action a_t ~ pi_theta(.| m_t, chat(h_t), a_t^{<i}). In EXPRAG-LoRA, the same retrieval pipeline injects the memory block into EACH training context so the model learns to leverage retrieved trajectories rather than memorize targets (retrieval becomes part of the supervised fine-tuning input). No latent-token injection; everything is text in-context.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-act with two variants. Static = one-shot exemplars at plan time: retrieve once, then run the multi-turn ReAct-style act loop with the fixed memory block. Dynamic = per-step interleaved: re-retrieve and refresh the memory block at every decision step using the partial history. No MCTS/tree search and no explicit hierarchical subtask decomposition; the policy directly outputs actions conditioned on retrieved experience + history. EXPRAG-LoRA additionally folds retrieval into the fine-tuning loop (retrieval-augmented training) so the trained policy natively conditions on retrieved trajectories at act time.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer/per-episode for static retrieval (memory block fixed across the whole multi-turn rollout) and per-step (per agent decision step / per tool-call-equivalent action) for dynamic retrieval, which re-queries and rebuilds the retrieved context at every environment step.
retrieved_item_representation: raw trajectory injected as text: full multi-turn chat trajectories (observation->user turn, action->assistant turn) serialized in chat JSON (default) / agentic JSON / compact JSON / textual formats and placed in a memory block in the system prompt, treated as plain text by the model. No distilled strategy/guideline, executable program/skill, or latent-soft tokens; the surface form is the verbatim trajectory.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: raw trajectory (lowest abstraction): the agent retrieves complete past interaction trajectories, not distilled strategies, insights, guidelines, reusable workflows, or procedural skills. The paper deliberately keeps memory as full unprocessed trajectories (read-only bank) rather than reflective summaries/abstractions used by methods like Reflexion/A-MEM.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Learned in-context robustness via training, not a dedicated filter. The index intentionally includes failures and suboptimal segments, and EXPRAG-LoRA (retrieval-augmented fine-tuning) trains the policy to learn which retrieved actions are relevant, so the model becomes robust to imperfect retrieved context through training rather than via a relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-aware preprocessing. The work also studies robustness to lack of relevant trajectories (Empty / Mismatched index stress tests) showing EXPRAG-LoRA degrades but, with a mismatched (training) index, remains often more robust than alternatives. No explicit retriever-aware contrastive training or reason-in-documents refinement.
memory_type: episodic (a fixed read-only experience bank of full agent trajectories). Explicitly framed as episodic memory in contrast to RAG's semantic memory. No skill-library, workflow, procedural, graph, or latent memory; no memory controller.
write_back: No (within the studied pipeline). Memory is a FIXED, read-only bank of full trajectories built offline from expert/recorded rollouts; the system does not write new experiences into memory during inference. The paper explicitly states it does NOT propose a new memory controller, online memory update rule, or reflection mechanism, and lists read-write memories as future work.
online_growth: No. The retrievable store is frozen after offline construction (from training-split expert trajectories or a small collected OOD reference set); it does not grow during deployment/test-time. Self-evolving / read-write memory with consolidation is named as a promising future direction.
write_back_trigger: never: no write events occur during inference. The index is constructed offline once (built from scripted expert trajectories of the relevant split, including failures), then used read-only. There is no on-success, on-failure, per-step, reflective, or human-validated write-back loop in the proposed method.
failure_experience_usage: Success+failure stored, but used as-is rather than contrastively. The retrieval index deliberately includes both successful AND unsuccessful (failed/suboptimal) episodes 'unless stated otherwise', so the policy can learn to identify which retrieved actions are relevant; the memory-block template separates successful from unsuccessful demonstrations. For LoRA/EXPRAG-LoRA supervised fine-tuning, only SUCCESSFUL trajectories are used as training targets. There is no explicit failure-only corrective-rule extraction; failures are retained in-context as negative/noisy examples.
memory_evolution_update: append-only / static: the bank is constructed once offline and never mutated, merged, refined, or pruned at runtime. No dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, forget-prune, or link-and-evolve dynamics; this is an explicit design simplification (fixed read-only memory).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/trajectory-selection is a fixed dense top-K nearest-neighbor rule (dot-product over frozen Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B), not an RL/value-optimized or learned retrieval policy. The novelty is training the POLICY (via EXPRAG-LoRA) to better USE retrieved trajectories, not learning the retrieval/selection policy itself.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private memory in the main experiments. The framework allows experience to come from the agent's own rollouts, OTHER agents, or expert demonstrations, and in practice uses scripted expert (environment-policy) trajectories as the shared source. But there is no mechanism for sharing/evolving memory across multiple cooperating agents or heterogeneous agent frameworks; cross-agent sourcing is mentioned as a possibility, not a contribution.
benchmarks: ALFWorld (Shridhar et al. 2021; household manipulation, binary success/failure, official held-out valid-unseen split, 6 task-types) and ScienceWorld (Wang et al. 2022; elementary-school science tasks, dense episode score in [-1,1] converted to binary success, official test split, 10 topics; subsampled to 5 variations per task except in the cross-paper Table 1). Each split partitioned into Easy (training/in-distribution) and Hard (held-out/out-of-distribution) task groups to probe generalization.
benchmark_family: embodied (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld) - text-based interactive embodied/decision-making environments.
baselines: Prompting baselines: Zero-shot, ReAct (Yao et al. 2023), ITP (Liu et al. 2026b, imagine-then-plan). Training-free memory-augmented: Mem0 (Chhikara et al. 2025), A-MEM (Xu et al. 2025), AgeMem-noRL (Yu et al. 2026), Memory Bank (Zhong et al. 2024), Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023). Supervised fine-tuned: NAT+ReAct (Wang et al. 2024c), IWM and Self-Reflection (Zhang et al. 2025b), ETO+ReAct (Song et al. 2024), SFT+ReAct, SAND (Xia et al. 2025), ITP_R (Liu et al. 2026b), Rule-based Expert. The paper's own baselines: EXPRAG (training-free retrieval), LoRA (SFT), LoRA+EXPRAG (inference-time), EXPRAG-LoRA. Internal No-RAG ablation. Backbones: Ministral 3-8B (main), Gemma 3-4B, Qwen 2.5-7B, Qwen 2.5-7B-1M (plus Qwen 2.5-3B in appendix).
key_metrics: Success rate (%) is the primary metric for both ALFWorld (binary episode outcome) and ScienceWorld (dense [-1,1] score converted to binary success at 1). Reported as mean over 3 seeds (2025,2026,2027) with std. Efficiency metrics (Appendix F): average prompt tokens/step, steps/sample, total generation time, time/step.
headline_result: On ALFWorld official valid-unseen, the simple LoRA baseline reaches 94.1% success (Qwen 2.5-7B), surpassing rule-based expert (89.6) and prior pipelines (SAND 85.0, ITP_R 85.1), and the training-free 'Best EXPRAG' reaches 83.6 vs <=42.7 for elaborate training-free memory systems. The flagship EXPRAG-LoRA result is on OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION (hard) tasks: e.g., Ministral 3-8B ALFWorld hard goes from LoRA 34.4 -> LoRA+EXPRAG 67.2 -> EXPRAG-LoRA 88.5 (with EXPRAG training-free at 47.5); Qwen 2.5-7B-1M ALFWorld hard 23.0 (LoRA) -> 91.8 (EXPRAG-LoRA); ScienceWorld hard for Ministral 15.6 (LoRA) -> 42.2 (EXPRAG-LoRA). Core takeaway: retrieval-augmented fine-tuning avoids the OOD collapse of standard LoRA while preserving high in-distribution success.
ablations: (1) Top-K sweep (K in {1,2,4}, Table 2/Tables 9-14): more retrieved trajectories generally help on ALFWorld (best all-task 41.04% at K=1 -> 64.18% at K=4 for Ministral) but saturate earlier on ScienceWorld (26.62 -> 34.67 -> 35.24); large K can hurt on hard tasks with mismatched index ('context rot'); K=2 chosen as default. (2) Static vs dynamic retrieval: dynamic helps when index is matched but is less stable under mismatch ('context churn'), can reverse at large K. (3) Index composition (easy/hard/all): mismatched index (esp. easy-index on hard tasks) degrades sharply; 'all' is the strongest overall compromise; benchmark asymmetry (ALFWorld benefits more from hard index, ScienceWorld opposite). (4) Backbone scaling: bigger/long-context backbones (Qwen 2.5-7B-1M) exploit larger K better; smaller models (Gemma 3-4B, Qwen 2.5-3B) noisier. (5) Trajectory formatting (Table 16): chat JSON robust default; textual hurts Qwen sharply at large K. (6) Prolonged fine-tuning / 'delayed generalization' (Sec 4.4.1, App D): OOD success keeps improving for many epochs after validation loss starts rising (grokking-like), best OOD checkpoints often near epoch 50; 9 epochs (ALFWorld)/29 epochs (ScienceWorld) used for main runs. (7) Robustness stress test (Table 4): Empty index makes EXPRAG-LoRA drop most (distribution shift); Mismatched (training) index is preferable to empty. (8) Caveat: Qwen 2.5-7B suspected ALFWorld data contamination (29.85% zero-shot vs 5.22% for 1M variant), so it is not treated as a main backbone.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task success rate is reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are reported separately, since the retriever is fixed/off-the-shelf and the contribution is on using retrieved experience, not on ranking quality.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (success rate). Some process-adjacent diagnostics are reported: average steps/sample (Table 17, where higher K reduces steps, i.e., the agent solves faster), prompt-token growth, and the training-dynamics analysis correlating (poorly) validation loss with downstream agent success. No formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported in Appendix F (Table 17, Ministral 3-8B / ALFWorld): average prompt tokens scale ~linearly with K (No-RAG 489.6 -> top1 1851.9 -> top2 3096.7 -> top4 5597.7 -> top5 6866.4), while steps/sample DECREASE with K (48 -> 34.4 -> 29.8 -> 25.7 -> 25), so total wall-clock time grows much more slowly (2769.59s No-RAG -> 2927.81s top2 -> 3556.04s top4 for 134 episodes); time/step rises (0.43 -> 0.73 -> 1.03s). K=2 chosen as best efficiency-effectiveness tradeoff. EXPRAG-LoRA incurs higher TRAINING cost (longer context) but preserves high in-distribution success. No dollar/API-cost figures (open models on a single 80GB A100).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-K, budget-capped by K: K in {1,2,4} studied, K=2 the default (captures most zero-shot gain while limiting prompt length/latency vs K=4); long-context Qwen 2.5-7B-1M benefits from larger K. The memory block of K trajectories is prepended to the system prompt; selection is fixed-K nearest-neighbor (no adaptive/precision-driven or reranked-then-truncated budget).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks). Data statistics (Table 5): ALFWorld easy train=1748/test=73 (look_at_obj_in_light, pick_clean_then_place_in_recep, pick_and_place_simple), hard train=1805/test=61 (pick_cool_then_place_in_recep, pick_heat_then_place_in_recep, pick_two_obj_and_place); ScienceWorld easy train=2335/test=1183, hard train=1254/test=636, with the test set subsampled to 5 variations per task (Table 6).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (dense top-K nearest-neighbor recall of past trajectories), Reuse: yes (trajectories injected verbatim as in-context exemplars / memory block, and via EXPRAG-LoRA the policy is trained to reuse them), Revise: no (retrieved trajectories are not adapted/revised per case; no execution-feedback case revision), Retain: no (fixed read-only bank; no online write-back of new cases)]. Effectively a Retrieve+Reuse system without Revise/Retain.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as experience retrieval / episodic RAG / retrieval-augmented agents (citing classic RAG: Lewis 2020, Guu 2020, Ram 2023, RETRO, Atlas, RAFT, and RAP/Kagaya 2024) and adopts the term EXPRAG from Wei et al. 2025. It does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use 'case-based reasoning'; it realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse under a RAG/episodic-memory framing.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; no tool/skill documents are indexed - the retrieved items are agent trajectories).
index_content_separation: N/A / No. No lightweight-index-then-content progressive disclosure; the trajectory key embeddings index the same full trajectories that are loaded verbatim into the memory block (no separation of a light retrievable index from heavy on-demand content).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (not a tool-retrieval system; environment interaction is via fixed text action grammars for ALFWorld/ScienceWorld, not MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful/function-calling tool stores; the retrieval index is a static read-only trajectory bank).
adaptation_mechanism: verbatim ICL exemplar reuse plus RL-free retrieval-augmented fine-tuning. Retrieved trajectories are reused verbatim as in-context demonstrations (no per-case LLM-prompted adaptation or execution-feedback revision). The key adaptation lever is EXPRAG-LoRA: supervised LoRA fine-tuning with the retrieved memory block in the training context, which trains the policy to adapt retrieved experience in-context to the new task (learn-to-learn) rather than memorizing targets.
builds_on: Classic RAG (Lewis et al. 2020; Guu et al. 2020; Ram et al. 2023 in-context RALM; RETRO/Borgeaud 2022; Atlas/Izacard 2023; RAFT/Zhang 2024) reframed from semantic to episodic memory; RAP (Kagaya et al. 2024, retrieval-augmented planning with contextual memory); the EXPRAG term from contemporaneous Wei et al. 2025 (Evo-Memory); LoRA / PEFT (Hu et al. 2022; Han et al. 2024); agent SFT/behavior-cloning (FireAct/Chen et al. 2023, Agent-FLAN/Chen et al. 2024); multi-turn agent serialization (Wang & Ammanabrolu 2025; RAGEN/Wang et al. 2025; Search-R1/Jin et al. 2025); Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (Zhang et al. 2025c) + Sentence-Transformers (Reimers & Gurevych 2019); environments ALFWorld (Shridhar et al. 2021), ScienceWorld (Wang et al. 2022); grokking/delayed-generalization literature (Wang et al. 2024a; Liu et al. 2022; Kumar et al. 2024).
contrasts_with: Standard LoRA/SFT fine-tuning (strong in-distribution but collapses on OOD/unseen tasks); RL/preference-based agent training (ETO, GiGPO/Feng 2025, IWM, Self-Reflection/Zhang 2025b) - the paper argues simple PEFT can already outperform these; complex training-free memory systems (Mem0, A-MEM, Memory Bank, Reflexion) - shown to add limited or even negative improvement vs simple episodic retrieval; self-evolving read-write memory and memory controllers (MemGPT, Memento, A-MEM) - the paper deliberately keeps a fixed read-only bank and does not propose a memory controller; Agentic RAG (Singh et al. 2025) - explicitly distinguished (Appendix A): Agentic RAG orchestrates multi-step retrieval over external KNOWLEDGE for QA, whereas this retrieves EXPERIENCE for policy generalization. Closest contemporaneous work: Wei et al. 2025 (inference-only episodic retrieval vs self-evolving memory on proprietary models) - this paper instead studies weaker open models under inference-time AND fine-tuning retrieval augmentation.
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience planning): an episodic experience-retrieval agent that retrieves full past trajectories in-context and, crucially, folds experience retrieval into LoRA fine-tuning (EXPRAG-LoRA). In the lineage of feedback/experience-driven planning agents (ReAct -> Reflexion -> ExpeL/RAP -> EXPRAG), it differs by (i) retrieving raw full trajectories rather than reflective summaries/insights, (ii) keeping memory fixed/read-only, and (iii) studying retrieval DURING TRAINING to teach the policy to learn from retrieved experience, positioning a simple read-only episodic RAG as a strong baseline that should be beaten before adding complex memory/RL machinery.
